title: Responsive images with `srcset` unexpectedly upscale when using `object-fit: none` or `scale-down`
body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? ### Summary When using `` with a `srcset` containing **width (`w`) descriptors** — especially without a `sizes` attribute, or with a `sizes` value larger than the physical image — browsers compute a **density-corrected intrinsic size** that may exceed the image's actual pixel dimensions. This value is then used as the image’s rendered size even when `object-fit: none` or `object-fit: scale-down` is set, which leads to the image being **upscaled**. This feels wrong to me, because one would expect these object-fit values to **prevent upscaling** and display the image at its natural size. ### Comparison with plain `src` and `srcset` with `x` descriptors If I omit `srcset` and use only a plain `src`, no upscaling occurs — even if the image is placed in a larger container. This is intuitive and expected: the image is displayed at its natural resolution, and `object-fit: none` respects that. **When I use `srcset` with `x` descriptors (like `1x`, `2x`)**, the behavior is also intuitive: no upscaling occurs under `object-fit: none` or `scale-down`. However, with `w` descriptors (especially with missing or overly large `sizes`), the browser computes a larger density-corrected intrinsic size and **renders the image larger** than its pixel resolution — even with `object-fit: none` or `scale-down`. ### Browser behavior Current browser behavior: - **Chrome** (as of recent versions) prevents upscaling with `object-fit: scale-down`. It uses the smaller of the container size and the image’s intrinsic pixel dimensions. This aligns with developer expectations, but is technically **not compliant** with the current spec. - **Firefox and Safari** follow the spec more strictly and upscale the image to the density-corrected intrinsic size even when `object-fit: none` or `scale-down` is set. ### Why this seems problematic - **Inconsistent**: Adding a `srcset` with no new information (or switching from `x` to `w`) changes rendering in unintuitive ways. - **Unexpected**: `object-fit: none` or `scale-down` should, in my opinion, prevent upscaling. - **Hard to control**: Developers must manually manipulate `sizes` or avoid `srcset` altogether to avoid unintentional upscaling. ### My interpretation of `sizes` and `object-fit` I believe the `sizes` attribute is meant to represent the **available layout space** an image will occupy — similar to how CSS `width` works. The acutal image dimensions are represented by the `w` descriptor. Therefore, I would expect `object-fit` to be allowed to constrain or override the density-corrected intrinsic size. When a developer explicitly requests `object-fit: none` or `scale-down`, they are expressing intent **not to upscale** the image — and that intent should not be overridden by image selection heuristics. This is especially noticeable with `sizes="auto"`, which effectively means “use whatever size is determined by CSS”. In that sense, it behaves similarly to using only `src` with layout-driven dimensions — yet with `srcset` and `w` descriptors, the image may still be upscaled, breaking the expectation of consistent rendering based on layout alone. ### Proposal Please consider adjusting the specification so that: - When `object-fit` is `none` or `scale-down`, the image’s **rendered size** should be clamped to its physical pixel dimensions (or the smaller of intrinsic and natural sizes in the case of `scale-down`). - The density-corrected intrinsic size should still be computed as usual, but `object-fit` must be allowed to constrain the final display size. This would bring consistent behavior across: - Static images (`src`) - Responsive images (`srcset` with `x` or `w`) - All relevant `object-fit` values ### Demo Here’s a CodePen that illustrates the issue: 🔗 https://codepen.io/zipper/pen/gvJBdp First image in each group represents the `src` only image, second is with `srcset`, third the same but in a narrow container and the last one uses an `x` descriptor. Note that the images using `x` descriptors behave as expected — **they do not upscale**, which highlights the inconsistency. ### Related issues - Firefox (closed as invalid) https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1974747 - Chrome (`x` descriptor, fixed) https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40648128 - Chrome (`w` descriptor, "fixed", but not compliant with the spec) https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41374573 - Safari (`w` descriptor, "fixed", but not compliant with the spec) https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=295203
